subject: FastCart: deployment mode follow-up — latency vs throughput tradeoffs
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Nguyen <sarah.ng@fastcart.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick post-call recap + one ask (latency vs throughput)

Hi Sarah —

Great to meet this morning. Quick recap from my side and a small ask so we can recommend the right deployment path (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC).

What I heard:
- Primary goal: power FastCart’s checkout personalization and fraud scoring.
- Traffic profile (from your team): 300 peak concurrent requests during promos; steady-state ~80–120 rps.
- Latency requirement: p95 end-to-end < 220 ms; soft target for p50 ~ 60–80 ms. Some payment flows are more latency-sensitive (checkout confirm).
- Data control: PCI-sensitive pieces will remain in your tokenization layer; no requirement for on-prem currently, but you want audit logs and VPC peering for production.

Quick recommendation (high level):
- Hosted API: fast to start, good for variability and cost-efficiency. Works if the p95 requirement can be met with our hosted SLOs + burst capacity.
- Dedicated capacity: better predictability for sustained 300 qps and tighter p95 tail; preferred if you want isolation and consistent latencies during promos.
- Private VPC: likely not needed now unless compliance demands expand; adds onboarding time.

Ask: can you confirm the p95 SLA target for checkout-critical calls (is 220 ms the firm target?), and whether the 300 concurrent number is sustained for >15 minutes or short bursts? A short answer will let us decide whether to propose a Hosted pilot with a fallback to Dedicated vs recommending reserved capacity up front.

I attached a short CSV template (fastcart_latency_profile.csv) — if you can populate the steady vs promo windows and the payload sizes for the most frequent endpoints, we’ll run a quick cost/latency projection and get back with a recommended pilot plan and a ballpark quote.

Next step from us: Karthik + Laura will run a model-fit check once we have the filled CSV and we’ll propose either a Hosted pilot with burst tuning or a Dedicated baseline.

Thanks —

Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

Attachment: fastcart_latency_profile.csv (CSV template: endpoint,avg_payload_bytes,steady_rps,promo_rps,promo_duration_minutes)
From: Sarah Nguyen <sarah.ng@fastcart.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ethan Park <ethan.park@fastcart.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick post-call recap + one ask (latency vs throughput)

Hi Jonas — thanks for the recap and summary. Confirming details so we’re all on the same page: 

- p95 target for checkout-confirm API: 200 ms firm (we can tolerate up to 220ms in exceptional cases).
- 300 concurrent = ~320 rps for 6–12 minutes during flash promos; steady-state 90–110 rps.
- Payloads: personalization request ~1.2–2 KB, fraud-scoring ~800 bytes.
- Compliance: we need VPC peering and audit logs, but keeping data in our tokenization layer is fine.

We filled the CSV (attached) and included a short example of promo vs steady windows. We’d like a recommendation that minimizes cost but ensures deterministic tail latency during promos.

Could you also include an estimate for a 3-month pilot (Hosted with burst tuning) vs a 6-month reserved Dedicated plan (monthly commit)? We’ll review internal procurement constraints.

Thanks —

Sarah Nguyen
Head of Engineering — FastCart
sarah.ng@fastcart.com | +1 (212) 555-0193

Attachment: FastCart_latency_profile_filled.csv
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Nguyen <sarah.ng@fastcart.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick post-call recap + one ask (latency vs throughput)

Thanks Sarah — this is helpful. We reviewed the CSV and sketched two concrete options. High-level notes first, then proposed next steps.

Summary of fit (based on your numbers):
- Promo bursts (320 rps for ~10 minutes): sustained tail-latency risk on Hosted if traffic spikes align across many users. Hosted can handle short bursts with autoscaling but tail p95 may be variable during noisy neighbors unless we tune isolation (higher cost).
- Dedicated (reserved pool): gives consistent tail latency and isolation during promos; recommended if you want a firm p95 guarantee during flash events.

Proposed options (ballpark; exact numbers after benchmarking):
1) Hosted pilot (3 months) — low friction, short lead time
   - Configure burst/autoscaling with prefix caching for personalization endpoints.
   - Add higher isolation tier during promo windows (temporary quota bump).
   - Expected median p50 ~ 60–80 ms; expected p95 range 160–240 ms depending on noise.
   - Pros: fastest onboarding, lower committed cost; Cons: variable tail unless we accept higher burst-price.

2) Reserved Dedicated (6-month commit) — higher upfront but predictable performance
   - Dedicated GPU pool (reserved) sized for sustained 320 rps with buffer.
   - Target p95 < 180 ms observed in our similar pilots.
   - Pros: deterministic p95; Cons: longer procurement and slightly higher base monthly cost.

Next steps I propose:
- Internal perf run: Karthik will schedule a short profiling run against a controlled harness (we’ll use your CSV payloads) — requires a brief test token from you (no production keys).
- Quote: Laura will prepare a side-by-side quote for a 3-month Hosted pilot (with burst tuning) vs a 6-month Dedicated commit.
- SLA/contract ask: I’m attaching a draft SLA excerpt for audit/audit-log expectations (FastCart_SLA_Draft_v1.pdf).

Requested from FastCart: a test API token (limited scope) and a preferred week for the profiling run. If you want, we can start the profiling this week and have an initial recommendation by Friday.

I’ll also include an internal note for capacity sizing.

—Jonas

--
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Nguyen <sarah.ng@fastcart.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick post-call recap + one ask (latency vs throughput)

Hi Sarah — looping in for scheduling and the technical plan.

Short plan and timing: 
- Profiling harness: we’ll spin up a short, isolated run that mirrors your promo window (10–12 min sustained 320 rps). We’ll exercise both personalization and fraud endpoints with realistic payload mix.
- Data we need from you: a scoped test token and confirmation that the harness endpoints are reachable from our test IPs (I’ll send IP range in a follow-up).
- Estimated run time: 2–3 hours to run the tests and validate results; 1 business day to produce a concise perf report.

Deliverables: 
1) Perf report (p50/p95/p99, CPU/GPU utilization, token costs)
2) Recommendation: Hosted pilot tuning vs Dedicated capacity sizing (including rough cost delta)
3) A simple mutual action plan with milestones (profiling -> pilot -> procurement)

Scheduling: I have availability Thursday afternoon (27th PST) and Friday morning — I’ll defer to Sarah. If we can run the harness this week we’ll aim to deliver the perf report by Mon morning and the Hosted vs Dedicated quote by end of next Tue.

Laura — I’ll hand over the baseline sizing after the run; can you prepare a template quote for both paths so we can fill numbers quickly?

Sarah — thanks again. If a Dedicated path looks necessary we’ll include a recommended buffer for headroom during promos (typically 20–30% over observed peak).

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Principal Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

> Attachment: FastCart_SLA_Draft_v1.pdf (excerpt: audit-log frequency, retention, VPC peering checklist)
